addedLines: - build-log-checker: Scan a Buildroot build log for failures and report which package broke, on which target. Use after a build run in the mx_SNMP_PLAN_E container when the log needs triage. Read-only — it never edits files or starts a build. (Tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- adr: Record and enforce Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) in Markdown under ~/mds4xgl3/.adr/. Use when creating or updating an ADR, when the user mentions ADR / architecture decision / .adr, or before making architectural or cross-module changes that could conflict with prior decisions.
- brainstorming: Turn an idea into an approved design spec through one-question-at-a-time dialogue, before any code is written. Use when the user invokes it explicitly, or asks to brainstorm, spec out, or design a feature or module up front.
- code-review: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/PRD asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- design-an-interface: Generate multiple radically different interface designs for a module using parallel sub-agents. Use when user wants to design an API, explore interface options, compare module shapes, or mentions "design it twice".
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- dut-console: Drive the serial console at /dev/ttyS0 connected to the Moxa MDS-G4000-L3-4XGS DUT. Logs in as admin/moxa, su's to root (password moxa) if at a Linux shell, runs the provided commands, and writes all I/O to ~/console_<date>_<time>.log. Use when the user asks to run commands on the DUT, verify behavior on the physical device, check device state via console, or snmpwalk/snmpset against the connected hardware.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- git-guardrails-claude-code: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- migrate-to-shoehorn: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.
- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the Obsidian vault with wikilinks and index notes. Use when user wants to find, create, or organize notes in Obsidian.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- qa: Interactive QA session where user reports bugs or issues conversationally, and the agent files GitHub issues. Explores the codebase in the background for context and domain language. Use when user wants to report bugs, do QA, file issues conversationally, or mentions "QA session".
- request-refactor-plan: Create a detailed refactor plan with tiny commits via user interview, then file it as a GitHub issue. Use when user wants to plan a refactor, create a refactoring RFC, or break a refactor into safe incremental steps.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- resolving-merge-conflicts: Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.
- rust-clippy-by-application: Use when MXNOS/buildroot Rust clippy scan fails under a pinned rustc (e.g. rustc 1.85, "rustc 1.85.0 is not supported", icu_*/bytestring/actix needing 1.86/1.88) because packages re-resolve crates without a Cargo.lock; or when converting per-package clippy scanning to per-application; or rolling out the per-package GitLab issue+branch+MR changes across many dl repos.
- scaffold-exercises: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.
- session-to-doc: Turn a whole Claude Code session (reference material gathered, the discussion in the middle, and the final conclusions) into ONE structured Markdown document that doubles as (a) standalone explanatory documentation and (b) a slide-ready outline. Trigger on: "整理這次 session", "把這段對話 整理成文件", "session to doc", "做成投影片大綱", "summarize this session into a doc", or after a /export transcript is provided.
- setup-pre-commit: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- andrej-karpathy-skills:karpathy-guidelines: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

### Task 7: `mx_portmirror` pilot — the §7 semantics migration

**Files:**
- Modify: `dl/app_moxa_framework/src/snmp_agentx.rs`
- Create: `~/WORK/SNMP_50ms/snmpwalk/RESULT-phase3-task7.txt`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 6's working GET path
- Produces: evidence that §7's value semantics survive the move — the thing Phase 3 exists to de-risk before Phase 6 moves all 567 event-config entries

**The MIB, counted from source** (`net_mx_portmirror.h` + its setup file): 18 entries, **RO 2 / RW 16**, arc root `1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1`, five URIs (`portMirror/portMirrorTable/` ×14 plus four scalars). Flags present: `REPLACE_TRUTH_VALUE` ×4, `URI_CONFIG_CHAIN` ×4, `URI_STATUS` ×4.

**Why this one is the hard case, and why it is not mxPortdb:** in Phase 2 the three `REPLACE_TRUTH_VALUE` entries turned out to be inert, because the ISS GET path ignores that flag (§7.1). Here `iss_build == 0`, so the framework GET path **does** consume it — MIB `enable(1)`/`disable(2)` against JSON `true`/`false`. This is the first time that conversion has to be reimplemented outside `entry_handle_generate_uri_value_file()`, and getting it backwards produces plausible-looking wrong values rather than an error.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write down the expected mapping before touching code**

For each of the 4 `REPLACE_TRUTH_VALUE` entries, record: OID, URI, current value read through the in-master path, and the JSON the status/config layer returns for it. That table is the oracle for Step 4. Capture it now, while in-master still serves these OIDs — afterwards the old path is no longer there to compare against.

- [ ] **Step 2: Register the arc and implement the conversions**

`REPLACE_TRUTH_VALUE`, `URI_CONFIG_CHAIN` and `URI_STATUS` are the three flags that appear on this MIB. `URI_STATUS` selects status layer over config layer; `URI_CONFIG_CHAIN` is the chained-config read. Derive each from the in-master implementation in `entry_handle_generate_uri_value_file()` (`ies_auto_mibs.c`), which is the behaviour being reproduced.

- [ ] **Step 3: SET must still work — it never moved**

The 16 RW entries still go to in-master. Round-trip one, using the Task 3 pattern from Phase 2 (read original, write, read back, restore, verify):

```bash
GET=/usr/bin/snmpget; SET=/usr/bin/snmpset; HOST=192.168.127.253
OID=1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.1.0        # portMirror/enable
ORIG=$($GET -v2c -c public -Ovq -t2 $HOST $OID)

1	---
2	name: dut-console
3	description: Drive the serial console at /dev/ttyS0 connected to the Moxa MDS-G4000-L3-4XGS DUT. Logs in as admin/moxa, su's to root (password moxa) if at a Linux shell, runs the provided commands, and writes all I/O to ~/console_<date>_<time>.log. Use when the user asks to run commands on the DUT, verify behavior on the physical device, check device state via console, or snmpwalk/snmpset against the connected hardware.
4	---
5	
6	# DUT Serial Console (Moxa MDS-G4000-L3-4XGS)
7	
8	This skill lets you (Claude) run shell commands on the device under test
9	connected to /dev/ttyS0 — without an interactive TUI.
10	
11	## Prerequisites (one-time setup the user must run)
12	
13	The skill talks to /dev/ttyS0 directly via `picocom`. The current user
14	needs the `dialout` group:
15	
16	```bash
17	sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER
18	# log out + log back in, OR run `newgrp dialout` in the current shell
19	```
20	
21	If you (Claude) call `run.sh` and the user hasn't done this yet, the
22	script will exit with a clear instruction. Tell the user the command,
23	do not try to `sudo` your way around it.
24	
25	## How to invoke
26	
27	```bash
28	bash ~/.claude/skills/dut-console/run.sh "<cmd1>" "<cmd2>" ...
29	```
30	
31	Each command is a positional argument. Examples:
32	
33	```bash
34	# Single command
35	bash ~/.claude/skills/dut-console/run.sh "uname -a"
36	
37	# Multiple — passed in order, prompt-synced between
38	bash ~/.claude/skills/dut-console/run.sh \
39	  "ip -br link" \
40	  "cat /etc/moxa/netsnmp/agentx_owned.list" \
41	  "snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost ifTable | head -20"
42	```
43	
44	The wrapper:
45	
46	1. Spawns `picocom -b 115200 --noinit --noreset /dev/ttyS0`
47	2. Wakes the console (sends `\r`) and detects current state:
48	   - `login:`        → sends `admin` + `moxa`
49	   - `$` prompt      → Linux shell as non-root → sends `su` + `moxa`
50	   - `#` prompt      → already root (Linux) or ISS privileged → continue
51	   - `>` prompt      → ISS CLI mode → continue
52	3. Sends each command, waits for the next prompt
53	4. Exits picocom cleanly with `C-a C-x`
54	5. Captures **all** console I/O (including login, password echo, prompts)
55	   to `~/console_<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>.log`
56	6. Prints the log path on stdout
57	
58	## Exit codes
59	
60	| Code | Meaning |
61	|---|---|
62	| 0 | Success — all commands sent, picocom exited cleanly |
63	| 1 | Bad args / no /dev/ttyS0 access |
64	| 2 | Login failed (wrong creds or unreachable login prompt) |
65	| 3 | Could not detect any prompt (device may be off/booting) |
66	| 4 | `su` failed (wrong password) |
67	| 5 | Timeout |
68	
69	## Tuning
70	
71	Default expect timeout is 15 s per response. For long-running commands
72	(firmware update, large snmpwalk on slow MIB), edit `set timeout` near
73	the top of `drive.exp`, OR pre-redirect the slow command into the
74	background and tail it on subsequent invocations.
75	
76	## What this skill is NOT for
77	
78	- Interactive debugging that needs you to read intermediate output and
79	  decide next commands mid-session — this is fire-and-forget per call.
80	- Anything that reboots the DUT mid-session (picocom drops on carrier
81	  loss; subsequent commands will be lost).
82	- Human-driven console use — the user's existing `mmmmminicom` alias
83	  (= `sudo minicom -D /dev/ttyS0`) is the right tool for that.
84	
85	## When to use
86	
87	Use this skill **without asking** when the user asks you to:
88	- "Run `<cmd>` on the device"
89	- "Check `<thing>` on the DUT"
90	- "Verify the new image actually works"
91	- "snmpwalk the device"
92	- "Show me what's in `<file>` on the switch"
93	
94	Always tell the user the log path you got back so they can inspect it.
95

```

The wrapper:

1. Spawns `picocom -b 115200 --noinit --noreset /dev/ttyS0`
2. Wakes the console (sends `\r`) and detects current state:
   - `login:`        → sends `admin` + `moxa`
   - `$` prompt      → Linux shell as non-root → sends `su` + `moxa`
   - `#` prompt      → already root (Linux) or ISS privileged → continue
   - `>` prompt      → ISS CLI mode → continue
3. Sends each command, waits for the next prompt
4. Exits picocom cleanly with `C-a C-x`
5. Captures **all** console I/O (including login, password echo, prompts)
   to `~/console_<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>.log`
6. Prints the log path on stdout

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success — all commands sent, picocom exited cleanly |
| 1 | Bad args / no /dev/ttyS0 access |
| 2 | Login failed (wrong creds or unreachable login prompt) |
| 3 | Could not detect any prompt (device may be off/booting) |
| 4 | `su` failed (wrong password) |
| 5 | Timeout |

## Tuning

Default expect timeout is 15 s per response. For long-running commands
(firmware update, large snmpwalk on slow MIB), edit `set timeout` near
the top of `drive.exp`, OR pre-redirect the slow command into the
background and tail it on subsequent invocations.

## What this skill is NOT for

- Interactive debugging that needs you to read intermediate output and
  decide next commands mid-session — this is fire-and-forget per call.
- Anything that reboots the DUT mid-session (picocom drops on carrier
  loss; subsequent commands will be lost).
- Human-driven console use — the user's existing `mmmmminicom` alias
  (= `sudo minicom -D /dev/ttyS0`) is the right tool for that.

## When to use

Use this skill **without asking** when the user asks you to:
- "Run `<cmd>` on the device"
- "Check `<thing>` on the DUT"
- "Verify the new image actually works"
- "snmpwalk the device"
- "Show me what's in `<file>` on the switch"

Always tell the user the log path you got back so they can inspect it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  #  OID                                  in-master GET   config JSON   mapping
  1  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.1.0      INTEGER: 1      true          true  -> 1
  2  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.3.0      INTEGER: 2      false         false -> 2

  4  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.2.1.12.* (no instance)   false x7      n/a — see §3

1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1 with the current config):

  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.3.0 = INTEGER: 2     portMirror/remoteSpanIntmedRole
  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.4.0 = INTEGER: 0     portMirror/remoteSpanIntmedVlanId
  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.5.0 = INTEGER: 0     portMirror/remoteSpanIntmedVlanIdSecond

                 "sourcePortRxTable":"00"x32, "sourcePortTxTable":"00"x32,
                 "sourcePortChRxTable":[], "sourcePortChTxTable":[],
                 "remoteSpanType":0, "remoteSpanVlanId":0,
                 "reflectPortMode":false, "sourceVlanRxTable":[]} ],
   "remoteSpanIntmedRole":false,
   "remoteSpanIntmedVlanId":0,
   "remoteSpanIntmedVlanIdSecond":0}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Finding: in-master publishes ZERO portMirrorTable instances
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The config layer has 7 rows. SNMP has none:

  snmpwalk    .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.2      -> No Such Object available on this agent
  snmpgetnext .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.2      -> .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.3.0
  snmpget     .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.2.1.2.1  -> No Such Instance
  snmpget     .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.2.1.12.1 -> No Such Instance

Two oddities worth knowing before Task 7 Step 5 reads a walkdiff:

  (a) The two GETs come back with a REWRITTEN varbind OID — the request's trailing
      index is dropped and the column subid is incremented:
        request .2.1.2.1  -> response .2.1.3
        request .2.1.12.1 -> response .2.1.13
      This is specific to this arc; a GET of a nonexistent OID elsewhere
      (.1.3.6.1.2.1.1.99.5.1) echoes the requested OID normally. Not caused by the
      host tooling — same result under `rtk proxy`.
  (b) /moxa/run/auto_mibs/ holds no portmirror value file at all, consistent with
      the table GET never reaching the file-generation step.

Row instantiation is not done in ies_auto_mibs.c: the table branch writes the raw
JSON to a temp file and shells out to /sbin/generate_uri_snmp_table (3715 lines, on
the DUT) to expand it into OID=value lines. Whatever suppresses these 7 rows lives
there, and Task 7 has to reproduce that behaviour, not just the truth-value mapping.

Consequence for Task 7 Step 4: only entries #1 and #2 have a value to compare
against. #3 and #4 can only be checked as "still no instance" unless a mirror
session is configured on the DUT.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Conversion rule, from source (both directions confirmed)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GET  ies_auto_mibs.c:2541  JSON "true" -> '1', "false" -> '2', anything else ->
                           error return, i.e. no varbind rather than a wrong value.
SET  ies_auto_mibs.c:2839  MIB 1 -> "true", 2 -> "false", anything else -> error.

Task 7 must reproduce the GET direction, including the "neither true nor false is
an error, not a default" part.

content.text:
The oracle is captured and committed. One thing came out of it that changes Task 7's shape, and it's the last moment to act on it — so I'm asking before opening Task 6.

**What's in the oracle** (`snmpwalk/ORACLE-phase3-task7.txt`, commit `d5f9241`):

| # | OID | in-master GET | config JSON |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `…603.5.5.1.1.0` (portMirror/enable) | `INTEGER: 1` | `true` |
| 2 | `…603.5.5.1.3.0` (remoteSpanIntmedRole) | `INTEGER: 2` | `false` |
| 3 | `…603.5.5.1.2.1.2.*` (entryEnable) | **no instance** | `false` ×7 |
| 4 | `…603.5.5.1.2.1.12.*` (reflectPortMode) | **no instance** | `false` ×7 |

Both directions of the truth-value mapping are covered by #1 and #2, so the 1/2 inversion Task 7 exists to catch **is** detectable from what I have.

**The finding:** in-master publishes zero `portMirrorTable` instances even though the config layer holds 7 rows (`sessionId` 1–7, all `entryEnable:false`). Row expansion isn't in `ies_auto_mibs.c` at all — the table branch shells out to `/sbin/generate_uri_snmp_table` (3715 lines, on the DUT). Task 7 has to reproduce *that* behaviour, not just the mapping. Two related oddities are recorded: a GET on `.2.1.2.1` comes back with a rewritten varbind OID `.2.1.3` (column+1, index dropped — arc-specific, not a host-tooling artifact, same under `rtk proxy`), and `/moxa/run/auto_mibs/` has no portmirror value file.

Also confirmed en route: `BUILD_TIME` = `2026_0805_1738`, two ESTAB pairs on `:705` (ISS pid 298, framework pid 3558). And a tooling note now in the file — `~/.local/bin/snmpwalk` is pysnmp and crashes against this agent; `/usr/bin/*` is the real net-snmp.

Task 7 Step 1 oracle — mx_portmirror REPLACE_TRUTH_VALUE entries, read through the
in-master (ISS) path while it still serves this arc.

Captured  : 2026-08-05 ~18:55–19:01
DUT       : 192.168.127.253, BUILD_TIME 2026_0805_1738 (Plan E)
AgentX    : two session pairs on 127.0.0.1:705 — snmpd(pid 2479) <-> ISS.exe(pid 298)
            and snmpd(pid 2479) <-> app_moxa_framew(pid 3558). Framework registers
            zero OIDs, so everything below is served by in-master ISS.
Tools     : /usr/bin/snmpwalk, /usr/bin/snmpget, /usr/bin/snmpset (net-snmp 5.8 on
            the host). NOT ~/.local/bin/snmp* — those are pysnmp-based and crash
            with "ValueError: too many values to unpack" against this agent.
Config    : read on the DUT, same source the in-master GET path uses —
            curl -H "Authorization: $(cat /moxa/run/auto_mibs/s_token)" \
                 http://127.0.0.1/api/v1/setting/data/portMirror
            (127.0.0.1:80, IES_URI_CONFIG_PATH = /api/v1/setting/data;
             Authorization header carries the raw token, no "Bearer" prefix.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The four REPLACE_TRUTH_VALUE entries, per source
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OIDs read from ies-auto-mibs/net_mx_portmirror.h, flags from
ies-auto-mibs/ies_auto_mibs_setup_net_mx_portmirror.c. Not copied from any MIB file.

  #  entry name                        URI / uri_index                          OID
  1  portMirror_enable                 portMirror/enable            .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.1.0
  2  portMirror_remoteSpanIntmedRole   portMirror/remoteSpanIntmedRole
                                                                    .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.3.0
  3  portMirrorTable_entryEnable       portMirror/portMirrorTable/ + entryEnable
                                                              .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.2.1.2.<idx>
  4  portMirrorTable_reflectPortMode   portMirror/portMirrorTable/ + reflectPortMode
                                                             .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.2.1.12.<idx>

#3 additionally carries URI_CONFIG_CHAIN.
Table index mapping: SNMP index N <-> JSON array element N-1 (ies_auto_mibs.c:2794,
`index = req_oid[last]; index--`). SNMP index 1 = sessionId 1 = portMirrorTable[0].

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. THE ORACLE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Both directions of the mapping are covered on both a scalar and a table column.

  #  OID                                 config JSON   in-master GET   state
  1  .…5.5.1.1.0      portMirror/enable  true          INTEGER: 1      as found
  2  .…5.5.1.3.0      remoteSpanIntmedRole
                                         false         INTEGER: 2      as found
  3  .…5.5.1.2.1.2.1  entryEnable        false         (no instance)   as found
  3  .…5.5.1.2.1.2.1  entryEnable        true          INTEGER: 1      induced
  4  .…5.5.1.2.1.12.1 reflectPortMode    true          INTEGER: 1      induced
  4  .…5.5.1.2.1.12.1 reflectPortMode    false         INTEGER: 2      induced

"induced" = produced by SNMP SET through the in-master path, then restored (§5).

2a. Arc as found, and as restored — these two walks are identical, which is the
    proof the DUT state was returned to baseline:

  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.1.0 = INTEGER: 1     portMirror/enable
  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.3.0 = INTEGER: 2     portMirror/remoteSpanIntmedRole
  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.4.0 = INTEGER: 0     portMirror/remoteSpanIntmedVlanId
  .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.5.0 = INTEGER: 0     portMirror/remoteSpanIntmedVlanIdSecond

2b. The one enabled row, full walk of 1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.5.5.1.2
    (session 1 enabled, reflectPortMode false, everything else left at defaults):

  .…5.5.1.2.1.1.1  = INTEGER: 1    index
  .…5.5.1.2.1.2.1  = INTEGER: 1    entryEnable        <- JSON true
  .…5.5.1.2.1.3.1  = INTEGER: 1    sessionId
  .…5.5.1.2.1.4.1  = INTEGER: 0    destPort
  .…5.5.1.2.1.5.1  = ""            sourcePortRxTable  <- JSON "0000…" (64 hex chars)
  .…5.5.1.2.1.6.1  = ""            sourcePortTxTable  <- JSON "0000…"
  .…5.5.1.2.1.7.1  = ""            destPortTable      <- JSON []
  .…5.5.1.2.1.8.1  = ""            sourcePortChRxTable
  .…5.5.1.2.1.9.1  = ""            sourcePortChTxTable
  .…5.5.1.2.1.10.1 = INTEGER: 0    remoteSpanType
  .…5.5.1.2.1.11.1 = INTEGER: 0    remoteSpanVlanId
  .…5.5.1.2.1.12.1 = INTEGER: 2    reflectPortMode    <- JSON false
  .…5.5.1.2.1.13.1 = STRING: "[]"  sourceVlanRxTable  <- JSON []

    Note col 5/6: an all-zero 64-hex-char JSON string comes out as an EMPTY octet
    string, while col 13's empty JSON array comes out as the two-character STRING
    "[]". Two different empty-ish JSON shapes, two different SNMP renderings.
    Task 7 must not normalise them to the same thing.

2c. Config JSON as found and as restored (identical; values abridged only where the
    7 rows are identical apart from sessionId):

  {"enable":true,
   "portMirrorTable":[ 7 rows, sessionId 1..7:
     {"entryEnable":false, "destPort":0, "destPortTable":[],
      "sourcePortRxTable":"0"x64, "sourcePortTxTable":"0"x64,
      "sourcePortChRxTable":[], "sourcePortChTxTable":[],
      "remoteSpanType":0, "remoteSpanVlanId":0,
      "reflectPortMode":false, "sourceVlanRxTable":[]} ],
   "remoteSpanIntmedRole":false,
   "remoteSpanIntmedVlanId":0,
   "remoteSpanIntmedVlanIdSecond":0}

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Row publication is gated on entryEnable — not on the row existing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The config layer always holds 7 rows. SNMP publishes only the rows whose
entryEnable is true. With all 7 false, the entire table subtree is absent:

  snmpwalk    .…5.5.1.2        -> No Such Object available on this agent
  snmpgetnext .…5.5.1.2        -> .…5.5.1.3.0   (skips straight past the table)
  snmpget     .…5.5.1.2.1.2.1  -> No Such Instance
  snmpget     .…5.5.1.2.1.12.1 -> No Such Instance

After `snmpset .…5.5.1.2.1.2.1 i 1`, all 13 columns of index 1 appear at once
(§2b). This is the behaviour Task 7 has to reproduce — a framework implementation
that publishes all 7 rows unconditionally would show up as 78 surplus OIDs, and one
that publishes none would pass a walkdiff against today's baseline while being wrong
the moment a mirror session is enabled.

Row expansion is not implemented in ies_auto_mibs.c. The table branch writes the raw
JSON to a temp file and shells out to /sbin/generate_uri_snmp_table (3715 lines, on
the DUT) which expands it into OID=value lines; the result is renamed over the temp
file. The file (/moxa/run/auto_mibs/portMirror_portMirrorTable_tbl) exists only
while a row is published — it was present with the row enabled and gone after the
restore, so it cannot be read retrospectively.

Two oddities worth knowing before Task 7 Step 5 reads a walkdiff:

  (a) A GET on an absent row comes back with a REWRITTEN varbind OID — the trailing
      index is dropped and the column subid incremented:

cd ~/WORK/SNMP_50ms

#!/bin/bash
# Wire-time latency for the mxPortdb OIDs that BOTH partitions serve.
#
# The 13 OIDs here are the ones known to be served identically by both
# partitions, so the same request can be timed on each and the results compared
# directly - which is what design doc 10.2's Phase 4 before/after needs. The
# index columns (column 1) are left out to keep the request set fixed across
# every measurement taken so far; do NOT read that as a partition
# discriminator. Mainline Build 2026_0805_1224 was measured answering
# .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.1.1.1.1.1.1.1 and ...2.1.1.1.1, contradicting the
# earlier note here that mainline serves none of them
# (see snmpwalk/RESULT-phase3-task1.txt).
#
# Captures with tcpdump (needs sudo), runs the GET loop, stops the capture, and
# pairs request to response by snmp.request_id. Client-side wall clock is not
# used: it includes snmpget's own startup (~3.2ms), which is not device cost.
#
# usage: sudo -v && tools/mxportdb_latency.sh <label> [host] [community]
#   label   goes in the pcap filename, e.g. planE / mainline
set -u

LABEL="${1:?usage: mxportdb_latency.sh <label> [host] [community]}"
HOST="${2:-192.168.127.253}"
COMM="${3:-public}"
ROUNDS="${ROUNDS:-100}"
GET="${SNMPGET:-/usr/bin/snmpget}"
PCAPDIR="${PCAPDIR:-$HOME/pcap}"

B=1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.603.1.1
# The 13 OIDs both partitions serve, port 1. Column 1 of each table is omitted
# on purpose - see the header.
OIDS="\
$B.1.1.1.2.1 $B.1.1.1.3.1 $B.1.1.1.4.1 $B.1.1.1.5.1 $B.1.1.1.6.1 \
$B.1.2.0 \
$B.1.3.1.2.1 $B.1.3.1.3.1 \
$B.2.1.1.2.1 $B.2.1.1.3.1 $B.2.1.1.4.1 $B.2.1.1.5.1 \
$B.2.2.1.2.1"

IFACE="${IFACE:-$(ip route get "$HOST" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.* dev \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)}"
if [ -z "$IFACE" ]; then
    echo "!! 找不到通往 $HOST 的介面；用 IFACE=<iface> 指定" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$PCAPDIR"
PCAP="${PCAPDIR}/mxportdb-13oid-${LABEL}-$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M).pcapng"

echo "介面 ${IFACE} → ${HOST}，${ROUNDS} 輪 × 13 varbind"
echo "pcap  ${PCAP}"

sudo tcpdump -i "$IFACE" -w "$PCAP" "host ${HOST} and udp port 161" 2>/dev/null &
sleep 2                      # let tcpdump bind before any traffic

for _ in $(seq 1 "$ROUNDS"); do

done

sleep 1

  if ($2=="0")                      { t[$3]=$1 }

}' | sort -n | awk -v L="$LABEL" '{v[NR]=$1}

#   .2.2.1.2.{1,2}   io/power/poe/status      two PoE power inputs
#   .2.3.1.2.1       io/di/status             one digital input
#   .2.4.1.2.{1,2}   io/relay/status          two relays
#
# The index columns (column 1) are not served at all, which is why they are not
# in the request set. Keep this list frozen across before/after or the two
# measurements are not comparable.
#
# All 8 entries are HANDLER_CAN_RONLY, so nothing here can perturb device state.
#
# Captures with tcpdump (needs sudo), runs the GET loop, stops the capture, and
# pairs request to response by snmp.request_id. Client-side wall clock is not
# used: it includes snmpget's own startup (~3.2ms), which is not device cost.
#
# usage: sudo -v && tools/mx_device_io_latency.sh <label> [host] [community]
#   label   goes in the pcap filename, e.g. before / after
set -u

LABEL="${1:?usage: mx_device_io_latency.sh <label> [host] [community]}"
HOST="${2:-192.168.127.253}"
COMM="${3:-public}"
ROUNDS="${ROUNDS:-100}"
GET="${SNMPGET:-/usr/bin/snmpget}"
PCAPDIR="${PCAPDIR:-$HOME/pcap}"

B=1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2
# The 7 status OIDs the agent actually serves. Column 1 of each table is not
# published - see the header.
OIDS="\
$B.1.1.2.1 $B.1.1.2.2 \
$B.2.1.2.1 $B.2.1.2.2 \
$B.3.1.2.1 \
$B.4.1.2.1 $B.4.1.2.2"

IFACE="${IFACE:-$(ip route get "$HOST" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.* dev \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)}"
if [ -z "$IFACE" ]; then
    echo "!! 找不到通往 $HOST 的介面；用 IFACE=<iface> 指定" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$PCAPDIR"
PCAP="${PCAPDIR}/mxdeviceio-7oid-${LABEL}-$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M).pcapng"

echo "介面 ${IFACE} → ${HOST}，${ROUNDS} 輪 × 7 varbind"
echo "pcap  ${PCAP}"

sudo tcpdump -i "$IFACE" -w "$PCAP" "host ${HOST} and udp port 161" 2>/dev/null &
sleep 2                      # let tcpdump bind before any traffic

for _ in $(seq 1 "$ROUNDS"); do
    "$GET" -v2c -c "$COMM" -r0 -t2 -On "$HOST" $OIDS >/dev/null 2>&1
done

sleep 1
sudo pkill -f "tcpdump -i ${IFACE} -w ${PCAP}"
sleep 1

echo ""
echo "=== 每個 request 的 varbind 數（應為 7）==="
tshark -r "$PCAP" -c 1 -Y "snmp.data == 0" -V 2>/dev/null | grep -c "Object Name:"

echo "=== 線上延遲（依 snmp.request_id 配對）==="
tshark -r "$PCAP" -T fields -e frame.time_epoch -e snmp.data -e snmp.request_id 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '
$3!="" {
  if ($2=="0")                      { t[$3]=$1 }
  else if ($2=="2" && ($3 in t))    { printf "%.3f\n", ($1-t[$3])*1000; delete t[$3] }
}' | sort -n | awk -v L="$LABEL" '{v[NR]=$1}
     END{ printf "%-10s n=%d p50=%.1fms p95=%.1fms p100=%.1fms\n",
                 L, NR, v[int(NR*0.5)], v[int(NR*0.95)], v[NR] }'

content.text:
I've hit a real design fork in Task 6 Step 3, and it changes what "no OID moved" means. Facts first, all from source + live DUT:

**The in-master path for `mx_device_io` isn't a pass-through.** `/sbin/generate_uri_snmp_table` is a Rust ELF binary (`dl/3rdparty_net_snmp/snmp_script_rust/generate_uri_snmp_table/src/main.rs`), not a script. It does the string→integer enum mapping the status layer doesn't do:

| URI | status layer JSON | SNMP | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `io/power/system/`, `io/power/poe/` | `"off"` / `"on"` / anything else | 0 / 1 / 2 | `main.rs:220-237` |
| `io/di/`, `io/relay/` | `"open"` / anything else | 0 / 1 | `main.rs:240-253` |

Live: system `["on","N/A"]`→`1,2`; poe `["off","N/A"]`→`0,2`; di `["open"]`→`0`; relay `["open","open",null]`→`0,0`.

**And in-master's published set is inconsistent in two ways.** The 8 declared entries produce **13 GET-able OIDs but only 7 walk-able ones** — every `index` column answers a GET and is skipped by GETNEXT. Worse, `io/relay/` publishes **3 index rows but 2 status rows**: the JSON array's third element is `null`, and `gen_value_io_relay_status` does `value_entry.as_str().unwrap()` on it (`main.rs:2483`) — it panics partway through the status loop after the index loop already wrote all three.

content.text:
哪一部分想先釐清？

我先把三個選項背後的事實補齊，你挑要追問的：

**關於「index column 可 GET 不可 walk」** — 我還沒查出成因。可能是 in-master 的 `namelen` / GETNEXT handler 沒把 column 1 排進去（那正是設計文件 D17 延到本 phase 的那個 invariant），也可能是別的。要不要我先查清楚再決定，會影響「這到底是缺陷還是刻意」。

**關於 relay 的 3 index / 2 status** — 我推斷是 `main.rs:2483` 的 `.as_str().unwrap()` 在 `null` 上 panic。但有個地方對不起來：C 側 `LibUtil_ExecShCmd` 失敗時會直接 return、不做 rename，那 GET 應該整個失敗才對，實際卻讀得到值。所以要嘛 panic 沒發生、要嘛 exit code 沒被檢查。我沒有實際驗證 panic，只是從原始碼推的。

**關於第三個選項** — 我不知道 snmpd 允不允許兩個 subagent 註冊重疊的 arc，也還沒查優先權怎麼決定。這個選項是我列出來的，可行性未經確認。

**還有一個我沒列進選項的事實**：這 4 個 URI 全部帶 `IES_FLAG_SNMP_URI_STATUS`，所以 Task 6 只碰 status layer，config layer 完全不涉入。in-process 讀取點是 `StatusOperation::get_status_from_path(plugins, path, userinfo, query)`；要接上去得把 `Arc<Mutex<StatusOperation>>` 和 `plugins_status` 從 `uri_service.rs` 傳給 subagent，也就是 `snmp_agentx::spawn()` 得從 `main.rs` 搬到 `uri_service.rs` 裡建好那兩個物件之後。另外 `UserInfo` 是純欄位 struct，可以自己組，但**要用哪個 role** 我還沒決定 — 權限檢查會走 `plugin.check_permission(userinfo, request_info)`。

content.text:
我前面那句話錯了，先更正：**不是「GETNEXT 一律跳過 index column」**。GETNEXT 鏈本身是好的 —— 從 `.2.1` 起走，index 跟 status 兩欄都走得到：

```
walk .…602.8.6.2.1  ->  .2.1.1.1.1=1  .2.1.1.1.2=2  .2.1.1.2.1=1  .2.1.1.2.2=2   (4 筆，完整)
walk .…602.8.6.2.4  ->  .2.4.1.1.1=1  .2.4.1.1.2=2  .2.4.1.1.3=3  .2.4.1.2.1=0  .2.4.1.2.2=0
```

真正的缺陷只在**跨 URI（跨 value file）那一步**：

| getnext 起點 | 回傳 | |
|---|---|---|
| `.2`（arc root） | `.2.1.1.2.1` | 跳過整個 system index 欄 |
| `.2.1.1.1.1` | `.2.1.1.1.2` | 同一欄內正確 |
| `.2.1.1.1.2` | `.2.1.1.2.1` | 同一 URI 內跨欄正確 |
| `.2.1.1.2.2` | `.2.2.1.2.1` | 跨到 poe，又跳過 poe index 欄 |

也就是：**每次踏進一個新的 value file，就落在該檔的 status 欄、never 該檔的 index 欄。** 所以從 arc root 起走只拿到 7 筆；正確的話應該是 14 筆（4 表 × 每表 2 欄 × 各自列數，relay 只有 2 列有 status）。我描述的是行為，還沒把 C 裡的成因定位到那一行 —— `fileBuffer_get_oidEntry` 的 `FILE_BUF_GET_NEXT_ENTRY` 是嫌疑點，需要再挖才能斷言。

relay 的 3 index / 2 status 不對稱則跟這無關，仍然成立。

這樣一來選項的代價變了：

content.text:
成因找到了，是缺陷不是刻意設計。兩段程式碼：

**觸發點** — `ies_auto_mibs_handle_file_buffer.c:224-227`。這個分支就是專門為「GETNEXT 落在比 table arc 短的 OID」寫的（註解寫著 `for reqOID(tableOID + '0', mxView) with getNext`），要回傳 `entry_pool[first_entry_index].file_oid_pool[0]`，也就是第一欄第一列。但它的 memcmp 比 `table_oid_len - 1` = **12** 個 subid，而 arc root 的 request 只有 **11** 個 —— 比對長度超過 request 本身，永遠不會相等，這條「回傳第一欄」的路徑對 arc root 根本沒機會執行。

**放大成跳過整欄的地方** — `ies_auto_mibs.c:1861-1869`：

```c

Task 6 Step 1 抓對照組時發現的。**不是 Plan E 造成的**，是 in-master (ISS) 既有行為，
在 framework 註冊零個 OID 的 Build `2026_0805_1738` 上量到。

## 現象

`mx_device_io` arc `1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2` 底下 4 張表，每張表 2 欄
（`index`、`status`）。從 arc root 走 walk 只拿到 7 筆，全是 status 欄：

```
snmpwalk .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2
  .2.1.1.2.1=1  .2.1.1.2.2=2      io/power/system/status
  .2.2.1.2.1=0  .2.2.1.2.2=2      io/power/poe/status
  .2.3.1.2.1=0                    io/di/status
  .2.4.1.2.1=0  .2.4.1.2.2=0      io/relay/status
```

但**往下一層起走就完整**：

```
snmpwalk .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2.1
  .2.1.1.1.1=1  .2.1.1.1.2=2      index 欄，walk 得到
  .2.1.1.2.1=1  .2.1.1.2.2=2      status 欄

snmpwalk .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2.4
  .2.4.1.1.1=1  .2.4.1.1.2=2  .2.4.1.1.3=3
  .2.4.1.2.1=0  .2.4.1.2.2=0
```

逐步 getnext 顯示斷點只在「踏進一個新的 value file」那一步：

| getnext 起點 | 回傳 | |
|---|---|---|
| `.2`（arc root） | `.2.1.1.2.1` | 跳過 system index 整欄 |
| `.2.1` | `.2.1.1.1.1` | 正確 |
| `.2.1.1.1.1` | `.2.1.1.1.2` | 同欄內正確 |
| `.2.1.1.1.2` | `.2.1.1.2.1` | 同一 URI 內跨欄正確 |
| `.2.1.1.2.2` | `.2.2.1.2.1` | 跨到 poe，又跳過 poe index 整欄 |
| `.2.4.1.1.1` | `.2.4.1.1.2` | 正確 |
| `.2.4.1.1.3` | `.2.4.1.2.1` | 正確 |

所以 arc root walk 應該有 14 筆（4 表 × 2 欄，relay status 只有 2 列），實際 7 筆。
被吞掉的 7 筆 index OID 用 `snmpget` 全都拿得到值。

## 成因

**觸發點：`ies_auto_mibs_handle_file_buffer.c:224-227`**

```c
if ( req_oid_len <= fileBuf_ctrl->table_oid_len )
{
    if ( memcmp(req_oid_list, fileBuf_ctrl->table_oid_list,
            sizeof(oid) * ( fileBuf_ctrl->table_oid_len - 1) ) == 0 )
    {   // 回傳 entry_pool[first_entry_index].file_oid_pool[0]
```

這條分支的註解寫明是為 `reqOID(tableOID + '0', mxView) with getNext` 準備的，要回傳
第一欄第一列。`table_oid_len` 由 `util_table_snapshot_setup()` 傳
`entry->oid_len - 1` = **13**，所以 memcmp 比 **12** 個 subid；而 arc root 的 request
只有 **11** 個 subid。比對長度超過 request 本身，永遠不相等 → 這條路徑對 arc root
形同不存在 → 落到 `entry_handle_exception()`。

`first_entry_index` 的設定（同檔 `:97-101`）是 value file 裡**第一行的欄號**；
generator 先寫 index 欄再寫 status 欄，所以它會是 1。意圖很清楚是要回 index 欄。

**放大成「跳過整欄」：`ies_auto_mibs.c:1861-1869`**

```c
next_subtree = netsnmp_subtree_find_prev( req_oid, req_oid_len, NULL, NULL );
while( next_subtree &&
       snmp_oid_compare(next_subtree->name_a, next_subtree->namelen,
                        reginfo->rootoid, reginfo->rootoid_len) <= 0 )
{
    next_subtree = next_subtree->next;
}
```

`<= 0` 會把**目前這棵 subtree 自己也跳過**。註冊是 per-column 的
（`moxa_snmp_handle_util.c:206-210`，用 `entry->oid_list` + `entry->oid_len` = 14
subid = table arc + 欄號），所以 `.2.1.1.1`、`.2.1.1.2`、… 共 8 棵 subtree。

`getnext .2` 被 net-snmp 派給 `.2.1.1.1`（system index 欄）→ 檔案查找失敗 →
exception → 跳過所有 `<= .2.1.1.1` 者、含自己 → 落在 `.2.1.1.2`（status 欄）→
用 `MIB_HANDLER_AUTO_NEXT_OVERRIDE_ONCE` 轉呼叫，回 `.2.1.1.2.1`。與觀察吻合。

**沒追完的部分**：跨表那一跳（`.2.1.1.2.2` → 實際 `.2.2.1.2.1`）照上述機制推應該落在
`.2.2.1.1.1`（poe index），實際又多跳一欄。嫌疑是 `gfileBufCtrlBlock` 是**單一全域**、
一次只裝一張表的 file buffer，但未經驗證。這一點不影響「這是缺陷不是設計」的結論。

## 判定

**缺陷，不是刻意不發布 index 欄。** 依據：那條短-request 分支的存在與註解、
`first_entry_index` 這個欄位本身、以及 index 欄用 `snmpget` 完全拿得到值 ——
若是刻意隱藏，GET 也該擋。

## 對 Plan E Task 6 的影響

Task 6 要把這 4 個 URI 的 GET 搬到 framework。若 framework 照 MIB 正確服務，
arc root walk 會從 7 筆變 14 筆，`walkdiff` 會報 **surplus=7**，全部是 index 欄，
且全部是修好上述缺陷的結果、不是回歸。計畫 Step 4 寫的 `missing=0 / surplus=0`
需要改寫成「7 筆已知且已解釋的 surplus」。

## 另一件不相干但同時發現的事

`io/relay/` 的 index 欄有 3 列（`.2.4.1.1.{1,2,3}`），status 欄只有 2 列。
status layer 回的是 `[{"status":"open"},{"status":"open"},null]`，而
`generate_uri_snmp_table` 的 `gen_value_io_relay_status()`
（`snmp_script_rust/generate_uri_snmp_table/src/main.rs:2483`）對第三個元素做
`value_entry.as_str().unwrap()`，在 `null` 上會 panic —— index 迴圈已經把 3 列寫完，
status 迴圈寫到第 3 列才爆。這是推論，未實際驗證 panic 是否真的發生。

content.text:
你的直覺是對的，而且推翻了我的結論。**我先前判定「缺陷、不是刻意」是錯的。**

`snmp_moxa_mib/private/mxDeviceIo.mib` 寫得很明確：

| object | MAX-ACCESS | 行 |
|---|---|---|
| `deviceioStatSystemPowerIndex` | `accessible-for-notify` | 125 |
| `deviceioStatPoePowerIndex` | `not-accessible` | 168 |
| `deviceioStatDiIndex` | `accessible-for-notify` | 211 |
| `deviceioStatRelayIndex` | `not-accessible` | 258 |
| 四個 `*Status` | `read-only` | 137/180/222/265 |

`not-accessible` 和 `accessible-for-notify` 依 SMI 都是**不得由 GET / GETNEXT 回傳**。所以照 MIB，這個 arc 只有 4 個 status 欄可取 —— 就是那 7 筆。**walk 的行為是對的**，`<= 0` 那條路徑雖然是我描述的那樣運作，但它產生的結果剛好符合 MIB。

真正跟 MIB 不一致的是**反過來那一邊**：`snmpget` 對 index 欄拿得到值，照 MIB 應該回 noSuchObject。源頭在 `net_mx_device_io.h` —— 它把 8 個 entry 全宣告成 `HANDLER_CAN_RONLY`，包含 4 個 index 欄，那裡就跟 MIB 牴觸了。

順帶驗到 enum 也對得上：`off(0) on(1) notApplicable(2)`、`open(0) short(1)`，跟 `generate_uri_snmp_table` 的 `gen_value_io_*_status` 完全一致。

# in-master GETNEXT 跨 value file 時跳掉整個 index 欄（2026-08-05）

Task 6 Step 1 抓對照組時發現的。**不是 Plan E 造成的**，是 in-master (ISS) 既有行為，
在 framework 註冊零個 OID 的 Build `2026_0805_1738` 上量到。

## 現象

`mx_device_io` arc `1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2` 底下 4 張表，每張表 2 欄
（`index`、`status`）。從 arc root 走 walk 只拿到 7 筆，全是 status 欄：

```
snmpwalk .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2
  .2.1.1.2.1=1  .2.1.1.2.2=2      io/power/system/status
  .2.2.1.2.1=0  .2.2.1.2.2=2      io/power/poe/status
  .2.3.1.2.1=0                    io/di/status
  .2.4.1.2.1=0  .2.4.1.2.2=0      io/relay/status
```

但**往下一層起走就完整**：

```
snmpwalk .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2.1
  .2.1.1.1.1=1  .2.1.1.1.2=2      index 欄，walk 得到
  .2.1.1.2.1=1  .2.1.1.2.2=2      status 欄

snmpwalk .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2.4
  .2.4.1.1.1=1  .2.4.1.1.2=2  .2.4.1.1.3=3
  .2.4.1.2.1=0  .2.4.1.2.2=0
```

逐步 getnext 顯示斷點只在「踏進一個新的 value file」那一步：

| getnext 起點 | 回傳 | |
|---|---|---|
| `.2`（arc root） | `.2.1.1.2.1` | 跳過 system index 整欄 |
| `.2.1` | `.2.1.1.1.1` | 正確 |
| `.2.1.1.1.1` | `.2.1.1.1.2` | 同欄內正確 |
| `.2.1.1.1.2` | `.2.1.1.2.1` | 同一 URI 內跨欄正確 |
| `.2.1.1.2.2` | `.2.2.1.2.1` | 跨到 poe，又跳過 poe index 整欄 |
| `.2.4.1.1.1` | `.2.4.1.1.2` | 正確 |
| `.2.4.1.1.3` | `.2.4.1.2.1` | 正確 |

所以 arc root walk 應該有 14 筆（4 表 × 2 欄，relay status 只有 2 列），實際 7 筆。
被吞掉的 7 筆 index OID 用 `snmpget` 全都拿得到值。

## 成因

**觸發點：`ies_auto_mibs_handle_file_buffer.c:224-227`**

```c
if ( req_oid_len <= fileBuf_ctrl->table_oid_len )
{
    if ( memcmp(req_oid_list, fileBuf_ctrl->table_oid_list,
            sizeof(oid) * ( fileBuf_ctrl->table_oid_len - 1) ) == 0 )
    {   // 回傳 entry_pool[first_entry_index].file_oid_pool[0]
```

這條分支的註解寫明是為 `reqOID(tableOID + '0', mxView) with getNext` 準備的，要回傳
第一欄第一列。`table_oid_len` 由 `util_table_snapshot_setup()` 傳
`entry->oid_len - 1` = **13**，所以 memcmp 比 **12** 個 subid；而 arc root 的 request
只有 **11** 個 subid。比對長度超過 request 本身，永遠不相等 → 這條路徑對 arc root
形同不存在 → 落到 `entry_handle_exception()`。

`first_entry_index` 的設定（同檔 `:97-101`）是 value file 裡**第一行的欄號**；
generator 先寫 index 欄再寫 status 欄，所以它會是 1。意圖很清楚是要回 index 欄。

**放大成「跳過整欄」：`ies_auto_mibs.c:1861-1869`**

```c
next_subtree = netsnmp_subtree_find_prev( req_oid, req_oid_len, NULL, NULL );
while( next_subtree &&
       snmp_oid_compare(next_subtree->name_a, next_subtree->namelen,
                        reginfo->rootoid, reginfo->rootoid_len) <= 0 )
{
    next_subtree = next_subtree->next;
}
```

`<= 0` 會把**目前這棵 subtree 自己也跳過**。註冊是 per-column 的
（`moxa_snmp_handle_util.c:206-210`，用 `entry->oid_list` + `entry->oid_len` = 14
subid = table arc + 欄號），所以 `.2.1.1.1`、`.2.1.1.2`、… 共 8 棵 subtree。

`getnext .2` 被 net-snmp 派給 `.2.1.1.1`（system index 欄）→ 檔案查找失敗 →
exception → 跳過所有 `<= .2.1.1.1` 者、含自己 → 落在 `.2.1.1.2`（status 欄）→
用 `MIB_HANDLER_AUTO_NEXT_OVERRIDE_ONCE` 轉呼叫，回 `.2.1.1.2.1`。與觀察吻合。

`.2.2.1.1.1`（poe index），實際又多跳一欄。嫌疑是 `gfileBufCtrlBlock` 是**單一全域**、

---
name: check-mib-max-access-before-judging-behaviour
description: 判定 in-master SNMP 行為是缺陷還是設計前，先查 snmp_moxa_mib/private/*.mib 的 MAX-ACCESS
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

要說某個 OID「walk 不到是缺陷」之前，先去 `dl/snmp_moxa_mib/private/<mib>.mib` 看那個
object 的 `MAX-ACCESS`。`not-accessible` 與 `accessible-for-notify` 依 SMI 都**不得**
由 GET / GETNEXT 回傳，table 的 INDEX 欄常常就是這兩種。

**Why:** 2026-08-05 查 mx_device_io 時，我從 C 原始碼把 `entry_handle_exception()` 的
`<= 0` 追出來，判定「index 欄 walk 不到是 off-by-one 缺陷」。使用者反問「.mib 的設計和
ies-auto-mibs 的行為不一樣嗎」，一查 `mxDeviceIo.mib` 才發現四個 index 欄全是
not-accessible / accessible-for-notify —— walk 不到才是對的，反而是 `snmpget` 拿得到值
那一邊違反 MIB（`net_mx_device_io.h` 把 8 個 entry 全宣告 `HANDLER_CAN_RONLY`）。
只讀實作原始碼會把結論做反。

**How to apply:** 遇到「某 OID 出現/不出現在 walk」的問題，MIB 檔是第一手依據，
ies-auto-mibs 的 `.h`（`.mode` 欄位）只是實作，兩者不一致時以 MIB 為準並把差異記下來。
enum 值也一樣可以拿 MIB 交叉驗證 generate_uri_snmp_table 的映射。
見 [[snmp-work-notes-repo]]、[[snmpwalk-diff-confounded-by-dut-config]]。

metadata:

要說某個 OID「walk 不到是缺陷」之前，先去 `dl/snmp_moxa_mib/private/<mib>.mib` 看那個
object 的 `MAX-ACCESS`。`not-accessible` 與 `accessible-for-notify` 依 SMI 都**不得**
由 GET / GETNEXT 回傳，table 的 INDEX 欄常常就是這兩種。

**Why:** 2026-08-05 查 mx_device_io 時，我從 C 原始碼把 `entry_handle_exception()` 的
`<= 0` 追出來，判定「index 欄 walk 不到是 off-by-one 缺陷」。使用者反問「.mib 的設計和
ies-auto-mibs 的行為不一樣嗎」，一查 `mxDeviceIo.mib` 才發現四個 index 欄全是
not-accessible / accessible-for-notify —— walk 不到才是對的，反而是 `snmpget` 拿得到值
那一邊違反 MIB（`net_mx_device_io.h` 把 8 個 entry 全宣告 `HANDLER_CAN_RONLY`）。
只讀實作原始碼會把結論做反。

**How to apply:** 遇到「某 OID 出現/不出現在 walk」的問題，MIB 檔是第一手依據，
ies-auto-mibs 的 `.h`（`.mode` 欄位）只是實作，兩者不一致時以 MIB 為準並把差異記下來。
enum 值也一樣可以拿 MIB 交叉驗證 generate_uri_snmp_table 的映射。
見 [[snmp-work-notes-repo]]、[[snmpwalk-diff-confounded-by-dut-config]]。

MIB 一查就把決定定死了，不用再選：**framework 只服務 4 個 status 欄，walk 維持 7 筆**，計畫 Step 4 的 `missing=0 / surplus=0` 照原樣成立。in-master 對 index 欄回 GET 那件事不複製 —— 那才是跟 MIB 不符的一邊，而且 walkdiff 看不到，要在 RESULT 檔明列。

已經進 repo 的東西（`~/WORK/SNMP_50ms`，都還沒 push）：

| commit | 內容 |
|---|---|
| `d5f9241` `52ec9ef` | **Task 7 Step 1 oracle 完成** — `snmpwalk/ORACLE-phase3-task7.txt` |
| `7649ea8` | **Task 6 Step 1 對照組** — `tools/mx_device_io_latency.sh`，p50 113.3ms |
| `6546cc8` `3967d0f` | GETNEXT 成因與**更正後**的判定 |

Task 7 的 oracle 四筆都有值了（表格那兩筆是我開了 session 1 induce 出來、量完還原，arc walk 與 config JSON 前後逐字相同）：`enable true→1`、`remoteSpanIntmedRole false→2`、`entryEnable true→1`、`reflectPortMode true→1 / false→2`。順帶更正計畫：mx_portmirror 是 **17 個 entry（RO 2 / RW 15）不是 18**，因為 `BCM_ROBO2_XSDK` 在這棵樹裡沒有定義。

Task 6 Step 2/3 的形狀現在也清楚了，計畫已寫進去：註冊 arc `1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2`（原計畫寫的 `…8.6.2.1.1` 是錯的，那只是第一張表的欄 arc），只服務 status 欄，並且要自己重做 `generate_uri_snmp_table` 的字串→整數映射（`"on"/"off"/其他 → 1/0/2`、`"open"/其他 → 0/1`，已用 MIB 的 enum 交叉驗過），`io/relay/` 第三列是 `null` 不發布。

接下來動工 Step 2/3。有一個我自己決定的點先講：in-process 讀 status layer 的入口是 `StatusOperation::get_status_from_path()`，它要一個 `UserInfo`；我會自己組一個而不是走 token 驗證，role 要挑哪個我會照 io plugin 的 `check_permission()` 決定，選好會在 commit message 裡寫明理由。另外 `snmp_agentx::spawn()` 得從 `main.rs` 搬到 `uri_service.rs` 裡 `status_operation` / `plugins_status` 建好之後 —— 這是唯一拿得到那兩個 `Arc<Mutex<…>>` 的地方。

content.text:
兩件事分開講。

**1. Arc root 是寫死的，而且只有這一個**

`register_arc(&[1,3,6,1,4,1,8691,602,8,6,2], PRIORITY)` —— 這個字面值會進 framework 原始碼。躲不掉，因為註冊的單位就是 arc（D3 / §4.2 決定整個 arc 註冊而不是逐欄），每個 pilot MIB 一行。

**2. 每個 OID 的中繼資料不寫死，走 ies-auto-mibs 的 .h**

那正是 Task 3 做的事。`lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs` 把 **snmpd 自己編譯用的同一批 `ies-auto-mibs/*.h`** 編成查表（1936 筆），Rust 端是：

```rust
lookup(&oid) -> Entry { uri, mod_uri, uri_index, iss_build, val_type, oid_index, mode, flags }
```

而且是 longest-prefix，GET 帶著 instance OID 也查得到欄位。所以 handler 是 `oid → lookup → 用 entry.uri / entry.uri_index / entry.oid_index 組出 status path`，沒有 OID 表寫在 framework 裡。`net_mx_device_io.h` 改了、重新 build，framework 就跟著變。

**3. 但有兩樣東西 .h 裡沒有，只能留在 Rust 程式碼裡**

- **字串→整數的映射**（`"on"→1`）。`.h` 只說 `val_type = SNMP_DATA_TYPE_INTEGER`，沒說 `"on"` 要變成什麼。C 那邊也一樣是寫死的，在 `generate_uri_snmp_table` 裡用 URI 字串 match。framework 這邊只能照做，一樣用 URI 當 key。

- **「index 欄不可回答」這條規則**。`.h` 把 4 個 index 欄都宣告成 `HANDLER_CAN_RONLY`，所以從 `entry.mode` 推不出來 —— 這就是它跟 `mxDeviceIo.mib` 牴觸的地方。

第 3 點的第二項有個具體的洞，你這個問題正好戳到：Task 3 已經加了 `IES_FLAG_SNMP_SYNTHETIC_INDEX`（`ies_auto_mibs_handle.h:92`），註解寫得很清楚 —— 「the table's header declares no column 1 - so no subagent can serve it and its GET must stay on the local path」。**但 device_io 恰好是少數自己宣告了 index 欄的 header 之一**：

```
4  net_mx_device_io.h      ← 本次 pilot
3  net_mx_turboring_v2.h
1  net_mxIpIfdb.h / net_mx_portmirror.h / net_mx_snmp.h /
   net_mx_syslogServer.h / net_mx_trap_notification.h / net_mx_trustAccess.h
```

全樹只有 19 筆是「宣告出來的 index 欄」，device_io 佔 4 筆。它們不是合成的，所以 `SYNTHETIC_INDEX` 不會被設上，Task 3 的 local/remote 分界會把它們**判成可以轉給 subagent**。那 framework 就得自己決定回什麼，而照 MIB 答案是 noSuchObject。

我打算在 framework 端用 `entry.uri_index == "index"` 當判別式回 noSuchObject，不動 ies-auto-mibs（Task 3 已經 commit 而且推上去了，為這件事回頭改 C 側的分界是更大的改動）。這對 Task 6 是安全的 —— 我已經逐條核過 `mxDeviceIo.mib` 的 MAX-ACCESS。但要當成通則套到其餘 15 筆之前，每個 MIB 都得同樣核一次，這點我會寫進 Task 6 的 RESULT 和 D19，留給 Phase 6。

要我照這個做法往下實作，還是你想把 index 欄的判別放回 ies-auto-mibs（例如宣告出來的 index 欄也標記起來），讓 C 和 Rust 兩邊只有一個真相來源？

content.text:
對，`register` 要帶 OID —— 但形狀跟 FRR 差一層，而且那個差別正好是現在的麻煩來源。

**FRR 的做法**：`REGISTER_MIB("mibII/ospf", ospf_variables, variable, ospf_oid)` —— 給一個 OID root **加上一張 `struct variable[]`**，每筆帶 suffix、type、ACL（`RONLY`/`RWRITE`）和 handler。net-snmp 拿 root + suffix 展開成完整 subtree，於是它自己就知道每片葉子的型別和存取權，**ACL 由 net-snmp 執行，GETNEXT 的走訪也由那張表驅動**。

**我們的做法**（`lib_moxa_snmp_agentx/src/agentx.c:186-196`）：

```c
reg = netsnmp_create_handler_registration("mx_agentx", mx_agentx_dispatch,
                                          (const oid *) arc, oid_len,
                                          HANDLER_CAN_RONLY);
reg->priority = priority;
netsnmp_register_handler(reg);
```

只有 arc root、一個 dispatch handler、整個 arc 一律 `HANDLER_CAN_RONLY`。net-snmp 對裡面有哪些葉子一無所知，arc 內的每個請求都丟進 `mx_agentx_dispatch`，型別/URI/存取權全部在請求當下才從 iesmap（由 `ies-auto-mibs/*.h` 編出來的那張表）查。這是 D3 / §4.2 「註冊整個 arc 而非逐欄」的決定。

兩個直接後果：

**存取權**變粗了。FRR 那種 per-leaf ACL 由 net-snmp 擋；我們只有「整個 arc 唯讀」。好處是 SET 自動留在 in-master（正好符合 §6.2 與 Task 7 Step 3「SET 沒搬」）；壞處就是你剛問到的 —— `not-accessible` 這種 per-leaf 的事在註冊時**表達不出來**，只能在 handler 裡自己回 noSuchObject。若是 FRR 的形狀，index 欄根本不會出現在 `variables[]`，net-snmp 連派都不會派過來，這個問題不存在。

**GETNEXT 現在根本沒實作。** 這是我看 dispatch 才發現的，`agentx.c:74-76`：

```c
/*
 * GET only. SET never moves off in-master (design section 6.2), and
 * GETNEXT across a whole arc needs the OID table that lives in
 * lib_moxa_ies_auto_mibs, so it is not this library's business.
 */
if (reqinfo->mode != MODE_GET) {
    return SNMP_ERR_NOERROR;
}
```

Task 2 當時把 GETNEXT 明確推給上層，因為走訪需要 iesmap 那張表。**Task 6 就是它到期的地方**：framework 一旦註冊了 `…602.8.6.2`，MODE_GETNEXT 進來會直接回「這裡沒有東西」，那個 arc 的 walk 會落到 ISS 的 per-column 註冊上（看 priority）或整個走不到。無論哪種，Step 4 的 `missing=0` 都不成立 —— 而且更糟的情況是 GET 由 framework 答、GETNEXT 由 ISS 答，兩個 process 的答案不保證一致。

計畫 Task 6 Step 2/3 只寫「註冊 arc、服務 GET」，沒提 GETNEXT。這是計畫的缺口，我認為必須在 Task 6 補上：在 framework handler 裡用 iesmap 做 GETNEXT 走訪（給定 OID，找出 arc 內下一個真正存在的 instance），而不是靠 ISS 接手。

**必要條件**：priority 必須小於 127。ISS 送出的 Register-PDU 用

priority 再相同就會 `MIB_DUPLICATE_REGISTRATION`，後註冊者失敗。**建議 priority = 100。**

但 priority 只解決 namelen 相同的情形，**不足以保護 in-master**，見 §4.4。

### 4.4 多 subagent 的註冊不變式

> 決策依據：D4b

未來若有第三個 daemon 註冊為 AgentX subagent（PDF 規劃過 fiber_check / lldp / dhcp_snp），
**priority 不是關鍵，`namelen` 才是**。排序鍵是 (`namelen` 由長到短, `priority` 由小到大)，
`namelen` 先比，priority 只在 namelen 相同時才起作用。

| 情境 | children 鏈 head | 結果 | priority 有效？ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 新 subagent 的 OID 範圍與 in-master **不重疊** | subagent | 該範圍 GET+SET 都歸 subagent，違反「SET 一律 in-master」 | 無關 |
| 新 subagent 的註冊 root 與 in-master **等長** | in-master（prio 100 < 127） | 設計成立 | **有效**（唯一起作用之處） |
| 新 subagent 註冊得**比 in-master 細**（OID 更長） | **subagent** | **in-master 被完全繞過**：SET 送到 subagent、GET 轉發不執行 | **無效** |

第三種是地雷。例：in-master 註冊 `1.3.6.1.2.1.2`（namelen 7, prio 100），
新 subagent 只註冊 `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8`（namelen 10, prio 127）：

```
1. new subagent  namelen=10  prio=127   ← head，in-master 永遠不會被呼叫
2. in-master     namelen=7   prio=100
3. ISS           namelen=7   prio=127
```

把 in-master 的 priority 調到 0 也救不回來。

#### 不變式（實作必須維持）

> **in-master 在每一個 subagent 註冊覆蓋的 OID 範圍上，必須有 `namelen ≥` 該 subagent 的註冊。**

只要這條成立，**多個 subagent 疊加本身沒有問題**。例如 ISS 註冊整個 interfaces group、
新 daemon 只註冊 `ifOperStatus`，而 in-master 兩段都有等長註冊時：

```
1. in-master(10, 100)      ← head，SET 與轉發都正常
2. new subagent(10, 127)   ← 轉發取到的第一個 AgentX，較細者優先，語意正確
3. in-master(7, 100)
4. ISS(7, 127)
```

`mox_snmp_forward_get_to_subagent()` 取 children 鏈上第一個 AgentX 節點，
自然就是粒度最細的那個，**不需要額外判斷是哪個 subagent**。

#### 偵測

`SNMPD_CALLBACK_REGISTER_OID`（`agent_callbacks.h:5`）在 `agent_registry.c:1285,1322` 觸發；
AgentX 註冊也走同一條 `netsnmp_register_mib()`（`master_admin.c:241`），因此會被攔到。
payload `struct register_parameters`（`agent_registry.h:37-48`）帶
`name` / `namelen` / `priority` / `session` / `reginfo` / `contextName`，足以判斷。

in-master 掛一個監聽器，收到 AgentX 註冊時檢查自身是否有等長或更長的覆蓋，

你貼的前案和設計文件是同一個答案，這不需要新決策 —— **§4.2 原文就寫死了**：

> in-master 對每個遷移中的 MIB 改用**整段註冊**（FRR `register_mib` 風格；表用 `netsnmp_register_table_iterator2`），取代現行逐欄位 `netsnmp_register_handler`。

所以你貼的 Plan E 前案（`register_iter_table`、`min_col..max_col`、`row_count` + `iter_handler`、RONLY、只服務 GET、SET 留在 in-master）就是設計文件要的東西。**偏離設計的是我們 Task 2 交出去的 `mx_agentx_register_arc`** —— 它用的是 plain `netsnmp_register_handler` 加自寫 dispatch，而且明確把 GETNEXT 推掉。CLAUDE.md 說設計文件贏，所以我把這個落差標出來而不是繞過去。

**GETNEXT 的缺口我追到會怎麼爆了**，比我原本講的更具體。`mox_snmp_forward_get_to_subagent()`（`ies_auto_mibs.c:3151`）**不檢查 mode**，而它的呼叫點在 `entry_handle_generate_*_value_file()` 裡，那條路 GET 和 GETNEXT 都會經過（`ies_auto_mibs.c:3339` 那個 `MODE_GET == reqinfo->mode ? TBL_GET : TBL_GET_NEXT` 三元式就是證據）。所以 Task 6 一註冊，in-master 收到 GETNEXT 也會轉給 framework，而 `mx_agentx_dispatch` 對非 GET 直接 `return SNMP_ERR_NOERROR` 不填值 —— 那些 OID 就從 walk 裡消失。

**改用 table_iterator 同時解掉 index 欄那件事。** 註冊時給 `min_col..max_col`，device_io 只註冊 col 2..2，net-snmp 永遠不會問 col 1；index 是 iterator 提供的 table index，不是被服務的欄位 —— 這正是 MIB 的 `not-accessible` 語意。不需要我上一則提的 `uri_index == "index"` 那種 hack，那個提議可以丟了。

另外兩個我先前漏掉、§4.2/§4.4 明文寫的條件：

- **priority 必須 < 127，建議 100。** ISS 用 `SNX_DEF_REG_PRIORITY = 127`（`snxdef.h:85`），net-snmp 本地預設也是 127；OID 與 namelen 相同再撞 priority 就會 `MIB_DUPLICATE_REGISTRATION`、後註冊者失敗。計畫 Step 2 的 code block 只寫 `PRIORITY` 沒給值。
- **§4.4 的 namelen 不變式**（D17 延到本 phase 的那條）：in-master 在 subagent 覆蓋的範圍上 namelen 必須 ≥ subagent。framework 用 per-table iterator（namelen 13）而 in-master 是 per-column（namelen 14），in-master 較長 → 不變式成立、SET 仍然留在 in-master。這點要在 Task 6 實測確認，不能只靠推。

我的建議是照 §4.2 做：在 `lib_moxa_snmp_agentx` 加 `mx_agentx_register_iter_table()`（包 `netsnmp_register_table_iterator2`）、Rust crate 對應加一層、Task 6 用它註冊 device_io 的 4 張表，col 2..2，priority 100。這比計畫 Step 2 寫的一行 `register_arc` 大不少，而且要動到 Task 2 已經 push 的那個 library。

要我照這樣往下做嗎？還是你想先把 `register_arc` 留著、只補 GETNEXT？

10	 * app_moxa_framework means one tokio task (design D5 / section 5.3). There is
11	 * no locking, and adding some would not make net-snmp reentrant.
12	 *
13	 * OID subidentifiers cross this API as unsigned long rather than net-snmp's
14	 * oid typedef, so the Rust FFI does not have to know net-snmp's headers. The
15	 * implementation asserts at compile time that the two are the same width.
16	 */

20

22	
23	#ifdef __cplusplus
24	extern "C" {
25	#endif
26	
27	/*
28	 * Session lifecycle. Call order is fixed: init -> register* -> poll loop.
29	 */
30	
31	/* Enable subagent mode and open the AgentX session. Returns 0 on success,
32	 * -1 on failure. Calling it twice is a no-op that returns 0.
33	 *
34	 * `socket` is the master's AgentX address, in net-snmp's transport syntax
35	 * (e.g. "tcp:127.0.0.1:705"). Pass NULL to accept net-snmp's compiled-in
36	 * default, which is the unix socket /var/agentx/master.
37	 *
38	 * This is a parameter rather than a constant because the address is a product
39	 * decision, not a property of this library: whoever writes snmpd.conf decides
40	 * it, and a subagent pointed elsewhere does not fail loudly - net-snmp keeps
41	 * retrying in the background and the session simply never appears.
42	 *
43	 * `ping_interval_secs` is what turns net-snmp's reconnection on, and it is not
44	 * optional in practice. With 0 - the default - net-snmp makes exactly one
45	 * connection attempt and never retries, so a subagent that starts before the
46	 * master is listening never connects, silently and permanently. With a
47	 * positive value net-snmp retries and keeps a ping alarm that also notices a
48	 * master that has gone away. */
49	int  mx_agentx_init(const char *name, const char *socket,
50	                    int ping_interval_secs);
51	
52	void mx_agentx_shutdown(void);

56	 * per-column: pass the arc root and its length. Registering finer than
57	 * in-master is what the namelen watchdog in ies-auto-mibs catches, and it

67	 * fds net-snmp wants watched and how long it may sleep.

70	 * or -1 on error (including fds_cap being too small). *maxfd is net-snmp's
71	 * own highest fd + 1. *timeout_us is -1 when net-snmp has no deadline, which
72	 * is the same condition as *block being non-zero.
73	 *
74	 * Re-query after every read and every timeout: the fd set changes when the

76	 */

 * lib_moxa_snmp_agentx - AgentX subagent shim for app_moxa_framework.
 *
 * This library exists to keep libnetsnmpmibs out of the framework process
 * (design doc D6 / section 5.2). It links -lnetsnmpagent -lnetsnmp and nothing
 * else from net-snmp; anything that needs the MIB tree does not belong here.
 *
 * Threading: net-snmp is not thread-safe and this library does not make it so.
 * Every function below must be called from one and the same thread, which for
 * app_moxa_framework means one tokio task (design D5 / section 5.3). There is
 * no locking, and adding some would not make net-snmp reentrant.
 *
 * OID subidentifiers cross this API as unsigned long rather than net-snmp's
 * oid typedef, so the Rust FFI does not have to know net-snmp's headers. The
 * implementation asserts at compile time that the two are the same width.
 */

#ifndef LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX_AGENTX_H
#define LIB_MOXA_SNMP_AGENTX_AGENTX_H

#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/*
 * Session lifecycle. Call order is fixed: init -> register* -> poll loop.
 */

/* Enable subagent mode and open the AgentX session. Returns 0 on success,
 * -1 on failure. Calling it twice is a no-op that returns 0.
 *
 * `socket` is the master's AgentX address, in net-snmp's transport syntax
 * (e.g. "tcp:127.0.0.1:705"). Pass NULL to accept net-snmp's compiled-in
 * default, which is the unix socket /var/agentx/master.
 *
 * This is a parameter rather than a constant because the address is a product
 * decision, not a property of this library: whoever writes snmpd.conf decides
 * it, and a subagent pointed elsewhere does not fail loudly - net-snmp keeps
 * retrying in the background and the session simply never appears.
 *

stays unserved without a special case. Only single integer-indexed tables are
supported; anything else changes this signature rather than the caller.

#!/bin/bash
# Run a command inside the buildroot tree in the Moxa Docker container.
# Usage: $0 <command> [project_root]
#   $1 = command to run (e.g. make 3rdparty_net_snmp-rebuild)
#   $2 = project root / container suffix (default: mds4xg)
# Example: ./run_in_docker.sh "make 3rdparty_net_snmp-rebuild"
# Example: ./run_in_docker.sh "make 3rdparty_net_snmp-rebuild" MYPROJECT

#DEFAULT_PROJECT="mds4xgl3"
#DEFAULT_PROJECT="NOS_v7.0_develop"
DEFAULT_PROJECT="SNMP_PLAN_E"

if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <command> [project_root]"
    echo "  command     = command to run (e.g. make 3rdparty_net_snmp-rebuild)"
    echo "  project_root = container suffix (default: ${DEFAULT_PROJECT})"
    exit 1
fi

CMD="${1}"
PROJECT="${2:-${DEFAULT_PROJECT}}"
CONTAINER="mx_${PROJECT}"

# Check if container exists
if ! docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qw "${CONTAINER}"; then
    echo "Error: container '${CONTAINER}' does not exist."
    echo "Please run your install/build script (e.g. bbbuild_*.expect) to create/start the docker first."
    exit 1
fi

# Start container if it is not running
if [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "${CONTAINER}")" != "true" ]; then
    echo "Info: container '${CONTAINER}' is not running, starting it..."
    docker start "${CONTAINER}" >/dev/null
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "Error: failed to start container '${CONTAINER}'."
        exit 1
    fi
fi

docker exec "${CONTAINER}" bash -c "cd /home/moxa/${PROJECT}/buildroot && ${CMD}"

content.text:
Build is running. Summary of where §4.2 landed while it compiles:

**Three repos changed, all committed on `snmp-plan-E2`, nothing pushed.**

| repo | commit | |
|---|---|---|
| `lib_moxa_snmp_agentx` | `0e85b01` | `mx_agentx_register_iter_table()` wrapping `netsnmp_register_table_iterator2` + a row-count callback; new `mx_agentx_table_dispatch` accepts `MODE_GETNEXT`, the old `mx_agentx_dispatch` still doesn't |
| `lib_moxa_rust_snmp_agentx` | `2058a15` | `register_iter_table` / `set_row_count_handler`, same double-box + `catch_unwind` shape as the existing handler; `cargo check` clean on host |
| `app_moxa_framework` | `a5bd7a3` | 4 table registrations, column 2 only, priority 100; GET served from the status layer in-process |

Three things worth pulling out of the diff:

**`min_col`/`max_col` replaced the hack I proposed earlier.** Registering columns 2..2 means net-snmp never asks for column 1, so `mxDeviceIo.mib`'s `not-accessible` index columns stay unserved without any `uri_index == "index"` special case. The MIB wins structurally.

**Row counting is `take_while`, not `filter`.** The iterator hands out row numbers `1..=count`, so the counted rows have to be the *leading* run. `io/relay/` returns `[{…},{…},null]` — `filter` would say 2 and then the walk would ask for rows 1 and 2 while the null sat at index 3, which happens to work here but breaks the moment a null appears in the middle.

**`status_to_integer` returns `Option`, and `None` means no varbind.** Not a default. The numbers are `mxDeviceIo.mib`'s own enums (`off(0) on(1) notApplicable(2)`, `open(0) short(1)`), which is why they agree with `gen_value_io_*_status()` by construction rather than by my having copied them.

Two judgment calls I made rather than asking, both documented at the site:

- **`UserInfo` role = `admin`.** The status plugin trait's default `check_permission()` returns `true` and `plugin_moxa_io` doesn't override it, so the role doesn't gate this read at all. `user` would be least-privilege but it's the one role the shared defaults in `plugin_agent.rs:54` / `plugin_config.rs:201` single out for refusal, and a future plugin refusing an SNMP read for *that* reason would be a confusing failure. The subagent can't write regardless — the registration is `HANDLER_CAN_RONLY`.
- **`snmp_agentx::spawn()` moved from `main.rs` into `uri_service.rs`**, after `status_operation` and `plugins_status` are wrapped. That's the only place both handles exist.

Still open on Task 6: the §4.4 namelen invariant needs *measuring*, not reasoning — framework registers at namelen 13 (the Entry node) and in-master per-column at 14, so in-master should stay head of the children chain and keep SET, but that's a prediction until I see it. Then Steps 4/5 (walkdiff + the "after" latency against the 113.3ms baseline).

file.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hot-swap freshly built binaries / shared libs onto the DUT without a
# firmware update.
#
# The DUT rootfs is read-only squashfs, so the files cannot be overwritten.
# Instead each new file is uploaded to /tmp (writable overlay) and bind-mounted
# over its original path. The swap lives until the next reboot.
#
# Usage:
#   dut_hotswap.sh [--host IP] output/target/usr/bin/app_moxa_framework ...
#   dut_hotswap.sh --restore [--host IP]
#
# Paths must be under $BR/output/target; the remote path is derived by
# stripping that prefix.

set -euo pipefail

BR="${BR:-/home/moxa/sdc1/home/moxa/SNMP_PLAN_E/buildroot}"
HOST="192.168.127.253"
USER="admin"
PASS="moxa"
SERVICE="app_moxa_framework.service"
RESTORE=0

FILES=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --host)    HOST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --service) SERVICE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --restore) RESTORE=1; shift ;;
        *)         FILES+=("$1"); shift ;;
    esac
done

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

# expect helper: scp a file, then run a script as root over ssh.
cat > "$WORK/drive.exp" <<'EXP'
set timeout 300
log_user 1
set host   [lindex $argv 0]
set user   [lindex $argv 1]
set pass   [lindex $argv 2]
set script [lindex $argv 3]
set files  [lrange $argv 4 end]

set sshopt "-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o PubkeyAuthentication=no"

foreach pair $files {
    set local  [lindex [split $pair "|"] 0]
    set remote [lindex [split $pair "|"] 1]
    spawn scp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
              -o PubkeyAuthentication=no $local $user@$host:$remote
    expect -re {[Pp]assword:} { send "$pass\r" }
    expect eof
}

spawn scp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
          -o PubkeyAuthentication=no $script $user@$host:/tmp/_hotswap.sh
expect -re {[Pp]assword:} { send "$pass\r" }
expect eof

spawn ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
          -o PubkeyAuthentication=no $user@$host
expect -re {[Pp]assword:} { send "$pass\r" }
expect -re {\$ $}
# root's login shell is zsh and its prompt is not a plain "# ", so sync on
# an explicit marker instead of the prompt.
send "su\r"
expect -re {[Pp]assword:} { send "$pass\r" }
sleep 3
send "sh /tmp/_hotswap.sh 2>&1\r"
expect {
    -re {HOTSWAP_DONE} {}
    timeout { puts "\n>>> TIMEOUT waiting for HOTSWAP_DONE" }
}
sleep 2
send "exit\r"
sleep 1
send "exit\r"
expect eof
EXP

if [ "$RESTORE" = "1" ]; then
    cat > "$WORK/remote.sh" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
# Only undo paths this tool recorded — the firmware has overlay mounts of
# its own (e.g. /usr/share) that must be left alone.
systemctl stop $SERVICE
if [ -f /tmp/hotswap_list ]; then
    while read -r m; do
        umount "\$m" 2>/dev/null && echo "restored \$m"
    done < /tmp/hotswap_list
    rm -f /tmp/hotswap_list
else
    echo "nothing recorded in /tmp/hotswap_list"
fi
systemctl start $SERVICE
sleep 5
systemctl is-active $SERVICE
echo HOTSWAP_DONE
EOF
    expect "$WORK/drive.exp" "$HOST" "$USER" "$PASS" "$WORK/remote.sh"
    exit 0
fi

[ ${#FILES[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "no files given" >&2; exit 1; }

# Build the upload list and the remote swap script together.
UPLOADS=()
{
    echo "#!/bin/sh"
    echo "set -e"
    echo "systemctl stop $SERVICE"
    echo "sleep 2"
} > "$WORK/remote.sh"

for f in "${FILES[@]}"; do
    abs="$(readlink -f "$f")"
    case "$abs" in
        "$BR/output/target/"*) ;;
        *) echo "not under \$BR/output/target: $f" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    remote_path="${abs#$BR/output/target}"
    base="$(basename "$abs")"
    staged="/tmp/hotswap_$base"
    UPLOADS+=("$abs|$staged")
    {
        echo "chown root:root $staged; chmod 755 $staged"
        # Drop a previous swap first so we always stack on the pristine file.
        echo "umount $remote_path 2>/dev/null || true"
        echo "mount --bind $staged $remote_path"
        echo "grep -qxF '$remote_path' /tmp/hotswap_list 2>/dev/null || echo '$remote_path' >> /tmp/hotswap_list"
        echo "echo 'swapped: $remote_path'"
        echo "md5sum $remote_path"
    } >> "$WORK/remote.sh"
    echo "  $abs  ->  $remote_path"
done

{
    echo "systemctl start $SERVICE"
    echo "sleep 5"
    echo "systemctl is-active $SERVICE || true"
    echo "systemctl show $SERVICE -p MainPID -p SubState --no-pager"
    echo "echo HOTSWAP_DONE"
} >> "$WORK/remote.sh"

expect "$WORK/drive.exp" "$HOST" "$USER" "$PASS" "$WORK/remote.sh" "${UPLOADS[@]}"

Honest status: Task 6 Steps 2–3 are implemented, build clean, and verified at the artifact level, but **they do not work on the device**. Here is what I actually know.

The status layer answers normally in that same process: `/api/v1/status/io/power/system` → `[{"status":"on"},{"status":"N/A"}]`.

**What broke:** every OID under `.1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.2` went dark — not just the index columns I meant to drop, but the seven status OIDs too. `getnext .1.3.6.1.4.1.8691.602.8.6.1` jumped clear to `.603.1.1.1.1.1.1.1`, skipping the whole region.

**The distinction that matters:** the GET returned `noSuchObject`, not `noSuchInstance`. A registered table with zero rows gives noSuchInstance. noSuchObject means the request never found a handler willing to answer — a different failure from the row-count bug I first assumed.

My leading hypothesis is the forwarding path, not the registration itself. in-master registers per column (namelen 14) and stays head of the children chain, so every GET *and* GETNEXT still lands on it first. It now finds an AgentX node beneath it, so `mox_snmp_forward_get_to_subagent()` fires — and as I found earlier, it doesn't gate on `reqinfo->mode`. Once it forwards, in-master returns `IES_GET_FORWARDED` and never produces the value it could have produced locally. If our side then answers nothing, the region goes dark in both modes. That fits the evidence better than my earlier guess that the registration displaced ISS.

But that's a hypothesis with a competing one — our table genuinely reporting zero rows — and they're separable. Rather than reason further, the next step is to instrument: log on entry to `count_rows` and `answer_get`. If they are never called, the request isn't reaching us and the fault is in the forwarding interaction; if they are called and return nothing, the fault is mine and the status read is where to look.

One thing I should flag about my own earlier reasoning: I claimed the §4.4 namelen invariant would hold because in-master registers longer than we do. That part looks right — in-master did stay head. What I did not anticipate is that being head is exactly what breaks this, because in-master forwards unconditionally once any subagent covers the OID. The invariant protects SET; it does not make GET work.

Nothing is pushed. The DUT is on the original firmware binaries with `/tmp/hotswap_list` cleared.

commit（都在 `snmp-plan-E2`，**未 push**）：

- `lib_moxa_snmp_agentx` `0e85b01`
- `lib_moxa_rust_snmp_agentx` `2058a15`
- `app_moxa_framework` `a5bd7a3`、`6ef8974`

## 為什麼改用 table_iterator（§4.2）

原本 Task 2 的 `mx_agentx_register_arc()` 用 plain `netsnmp_register_handler`，
net-snmp 對這種註冊**不提供 GETNEXT 支援**，`mx_agentx_dispatch()` 只好拒收
非 MODE_GET。設計文件 §4.2 早就寫明「表用 `netsnmp_register_table_iterator2`」，
所以偏離設計的是 Task 2 的 shim，不是這個決定。

順帶解掉 index 欄的問題：註冊時給 `min_col..max_col` = 2..2，net-snmp 永遠不會問
col 1，`mxDeviceIo.mib` 的 not-accessible 語意就結構性地成立，不需要
`uri_index == "index"` 那種判別式。

**成功的部分**（都有證據，不是推論）：

- 四次 `register_iter_table` 全部回成功
- framework log：`AgentX registered 4 mx_device_io tables, column 2 only, priority 100`
- log 同時印 `ping 5s`（舊 image 是 15s）→ 確認跑的是新 binary
- 服務 active、pid 1311、`NRestarts=0` → `run_subagent` 沒有回錯（回錯會 drop
  Session 進而 `mx_agentx_shutdown`）
- 同一個 process 的 status layer 正常：
